t: This is Queen Anne Street, a street in the City of Westminster. It takes its name from Queen Anne, who ruled England, Scotland and Ireland from 1702, and became Queen of Great Britain and Ireland after the Acts of Union in 1707. She reigned until her death in 1714. Sir Thomas Dyke Acland, a politician and barrister, was born on this street in 1842. He was a large landowner from Devon, and he insisted on being called Sir Thomas in public, rather than the Charlie his family used.
